formula: log1p|EMA_k| - log1p(||DR||), k in {EMAi, EMAd} x alpha {0.001, 0.01, 0.1}  (6 per sensor)
rationale: Transient (EMA) amplitude relative to the steady-state amplitude of the same sensor: a response-shape descriptor that cancels the common concentration scale to first order. Built from one sensor only.
references: EMA feature definition: Fonollosa, Rodriguez-Lujan, Huerta, Data in Brief 2015 (PMC4510048). Transient features carry gas identity: Muezzinoglu et al., Sens. Actuators B 137(2):507-512, 2009 (title and venue verified, text not read). Normalisation by a reference response: Yan et al., Sensors 15(11):27804, 2015 (doi 10.3390/s151127804). The exact ratio is our construction.

formula: log1p|EMA(0.1)| - log1p|EMA(0.001)| for the rising and the decaying part  (2 per sensor)
rationale: alpha sets the time scale of the EMA: 0.1 follows the fast part of the response, 0.001 the slow part. Their ratio describes the response kinetics (adsorption/desorption speed) independently of amplitude. Built from one sensor only.
references: EMA definition: Fonollosa et al. 2015 (Data in Brief). Use of transient features: Muezzinoglu et al. 2009 (as above). The exact ratio is our construction; no reference proposes it.
